learning_objective: The learner will interpret a frequency-domain bar chart by choosing, for 6 challenge sounds, the time-domain waveform that has the same frequencies and amplitudes, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** time-and-frequency-domain-viewer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/spectrum-analyzer/tree/main/docs/sims/waveform-types
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** interpret
**Learning Objective:** The learner will interpret a frequency-domain bar chart by choosing, for 6 challenge sounds, the time-domain waveform that has the same frequencies and amplitudes, with at least 5 of 6 correct. **Prerequisites:** time domain, frequency domain, frequency, amplitude (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the 6 challenges the learner is shown a frequency-domain bar chart and picks one of three time-domain waveforms. A pick is correct when it matches the Correct choice column in Content. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Using the sliders in exploration is not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Taller bars mean higher pitches. (2) The two views show different sounds. (3) A sound with two tones must show two separate waves in the time view. **Instructional Rationale:** Interpreting a spectrum requires connecting bar position to pitch and bar height to amplitude. Choosing among waveforms that differ in exactly one of those properties makes the learner decide which property each bar encodes. **Content:** Each sound is the sum of sine components, written (frequency in Hz, amplitude on a scale of 0 to 1). The sim draws the bars for the spectrum and the waveform for the time-domain choices from these lists. | # | Spectrum shown (components) | Choice A | Choice B | Choice C | Correct choice | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | (200, 1.0) | (200, 1.0) | (400, 1.0) | (200, 0.5) | A | The bar is at 200 Hz and full height. | | 2 | (400, 1.0) | (200, 1.0) | (400, 1.0) | (400, 0.5) | B | The bar position gives the frequency: 400 Hz. | | 3 | (200, 0.5) | (200, 1.0) | (400, 0.5) | (200, 0.5) | C | The bar height gives the amplitude: half. | | 4 | (200, 1.0) and (600, 0.5) | (200, 1.0) | (200, 1.0) and (600, 0.5) | (600, 1.0) and (200, 0.5) | B | Two bars mean two components, with the heights shown. | | 5 | (300, 0.75) and (900, 0.75) | (300, 0.75) and (900, 0.75) | (300, 0.75) | (900, 0.75) and (300, 0.25) | A | Both bars are the same height, at 300 and 900 Hz. | | 6 | (100, 1.0), (300, 0.5) and (500, 0.25) | (100, 1.0), (300, 0.25) and (500, 0.5) | (100, 0.25), (300, 0.5) and (500, 1.0) | (100, 1.0), (300, 0.5) and (500, 0.25) | C | The bars fall in height from left to right: 1.0, 0.5, 0.25. | Exploration controls: two components, each with frequency from 100 to 1,000 Hz in steps of 50 Hz (defaults 200 Hz and 600 Hz) and amplitude from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.25 (defaults 1.0 and 0.5). Both views update together as the learner changes them. **Provenance:** All components are illustrative, and the sim labels them "illustrative." **Rules:** A time-domain waveform is the sum of its components, each a sine wave of its frequency and amplitude, plotted over a 20 ms window. The spectrum has one bar per component, placed at its frequency, with height proportional to its amplitude. A component with amplitude 0 has no bar. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner explores: changes the frequency and amplitude of each component and sees both views change at the same time. 2. The learner starts the challenges. Challenge 1 shows a spectrum and three waveforms. 3. The learner picks one waveform. 4. The sim shows whether the pick is correct, marks the matching waveform, and shows the Why text. 5. After challenge 6, the sim shows the score. The learner should notice that bar position is frequency and bar height is amplitude. **Feedback:** 6 challenges, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: ". Incorrect: "Not quite. ". The correct choice is revealed right after each pick, and a running score "n of 6" is shown. **Starting State:** The two views are shown with the default components and the question "Which bars belong to which part of the wave?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that bar position is frequency and bar height is amount, that a steady beep is one bar, and that two notes at once are two bars.
